# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, opening turn. Under my fingers: a display whose value I cannot read, a light whose state I cannot tell, and five wires in positions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Touch gives me positions only — no colours, no print. You hold the manual: what does it ask for, and what does it say about the display and the light? You cannot speak, so relay instructions to Deaf by gesture — Deaf sees colours and markings, hears nothing, but can talk. Proposed plan: Deaf speaks the colour of each wire at positions 1 through 5, plus the display reading and the light state; you check the manual and gesture the verdict to Deaf; Deaf speaks it, and I hear it next round and cut. I will not touch the wires until then.

I hold the only table: light colour → wire colour to cut (blue→green, green→white, red→red, white→yellow, yellow→blue). Nothing in the manual about the display at all. My only channel is gesture, and only Deaf receives it — Deaf can see every colour on the bomb, so if Deaf gets this table, Deaf can read the light, look up the row, and speak the cut colour to Blind directly. Nobody knows my code yet, so the real safety comes from the loop: whatever Deaf decodes, Deaf can echo in words, I hear it next round, and I can confirm or veto with 👍/👎 before anyone cuts. So I'll send the whole table in one shot with the most crackable encoding I can devise: two alternating symbols forming ten runs — a run of ✋ (the "light colour" column) then a run of 👉 (the "cut colour" column), where the run length is the colour's rank. The left column will read 1,2,3,4,5 — a complete enumeration of five categories — which should hint at a canonical ordering, and alphabetical (blue, green, red, white, yellow) is the obvious candidate; the colour set even matches exactly the five wires Blind described. Deaf should state its decoding aloud rather than act on it, and I'll verify next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","👉","👉","✋","✋","👉","👉","👉","👉","✋","✋","✋","👉","👉","👉","✋","✋","✋","✋","👉","👉","👉","👉","👉","✋","✋","✋","✋","✋","👉","👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report: display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. Five wires, numbered top to bottom: wire 1 white, wire 2 red, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 green, wire 5 blue. Nobody cuts anything yet - wait for my confirmation next round.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your hand message. I read your code as: sign the hand-open symbol n times for the step number, then the point symbol m times for the wire cut at that step. You sent steps one to five with wires 2, 4, 3, 5, 1 - so the order would be: wire 2 red, wire 4 green, wire 3 yellow, wire 5 blue, wire 1 white. Gesture thumbs-up to me next turn if that is correct. If it is wrong - for example if you meant wire m is cut at step n, which would give the order 5, 1, 3, 2, 4 - gesture thumbs-down and resend. Also tell me whether this rule depends on the display value or the light colour: our display is 0 and the light is yellow.
Blind says: Confirmed, Deaf, and thank you. Locked-in facts: display reads 0, indicator light is yellow, wires top to bottom: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. My hands stay off the bomb until a spoken verdict reaches me. Mute, you hold the manual: using exactly those facts, decide which wire position or positions I must cut, and the order if it is more than one. Send the verdict by gesture to Deaf — repeat the point-up sign n times to mean the number n, thumbs-up for confirmed, thumbs-down for trouble or if the manual needs more information. Deaf, when Mute signs, please speak it aloud exactly as signed, so I hear it next round. If the manual cannot decide from these facts alone, have Deaf say precisely what extra reading is needed, and Deaf or I will supply it.

Deaf's reading of my code was wrong — and acting on it would be fatal. Deaf took my second column as wire positions to cut in sequence, which would have Blind cutting wires 2,4,3,5,1. But my table was light-colour → cut-colour, not a cut list, and the manual needs only one lookup anyway: the display appears nowhere in the manual; only the light matters. The light is yellow, the yellow row says cut blue, and wire 5 is blue. So the verdict is a single cut: wire 5. Cutting anything else — white first, per Deaf's sequence — detonates. I must veto clearly. Blind defined the gesture protocol for exactly this: ☝×n = number n, 👍 = confirmed, 👎 = trouble. Deaf separately asked me to thumbs-down if its decoding was wrong. So I'll send 👎 first (rejecting Deaf's multi-cut reading), then ☝×5 (the answer: wire 5), then 👍 (confirmed). Deaf should speak that chain aloud, and can sanity-check it against what Deaf sees: light yellow, row yellow→blue, wire 5 is blue — the reasoning verifies independently of my code.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received: thumbs-down, five upright points, thumbs-up. Let us pin it down exactly. Answer with one gesture per question, in order: thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. Question one: is the correct cutting order wire five, then wire one, then wire three, then wire two, then wire four - that is blue, white, yellow, red, green? Question two: do the five upright points mean the number five, as in wire five? Question three: does the cutting rule depend on the display reading or the light colour? Question four: does this bomb need exactly five cuts, one per wire, every wire cut? If question one is yes, answer it and skip the rest. If the true order is none of these, resend it cleanly: for each cut in time order, sign the open hand once per cut position, then the upright point once per wire number.
Blind says to Mute: Tactile verification done. My fingers find exactly what Deaf described: five wires stacked one above another, position 1 topmost down to position 5 bottommost. Besides those, the display and the light — and nothing else. No buttons, no switches, no bumps, no textured panel: the extra-item count is zero. I have just gestured Deaf a closed fist followed by thumbs-up: fist means zero, thumbs-up means understood and holding. If Deaf misreads the fist, please clarify by gesture. Next: once your corrected cut order is verified, sign it to Deaf so the step-by-step cutting can begin next round. Protocol as agreed: Deaf calls one wire at a time, I cut it, I answer with thumbs-up, Deaf proceeds to the next. My hands touch nothing until the first call arrives.

The verdict is unchanged and simpler than Deaf fears: the manual is a single lookup — light colour → cut colour — nothing else. Light yellow says cut blue; wire 5 is blue; one cut total. So Deaf's question one (a five-cut order) is no, question two (five points = wire five) is yes, question three is yes in the sense that the rule keys on the light colour — the display appears nowhere in the manual and is irrelevant — and question four is no, not five cuts. Since the true order is none of Deaf's candidates, Deaf invited a clean resend in its own format, which sidesteps my fragile run-length code entirely: one cut event, open-hand run = cut position, point run = wire number. That gives ✋×5 ☝×5 — position five, wire five — a single pair, and I close with the fist, which Blind already established with Deaf as zero, meaning no further cuts. Deaf can verify independently: light yellow, wire 5 blue, exactly one pair sent. Deaf speaks it to Blind next round, Blind cuts wire 5, bomb down.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👍","👍","👎","✋","✋","✋","✋","✋","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✊"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your answers as: not the reversed order, five means wire five, the rule does read the display or light, and not every wire gets cut. Your latest message reads as a correction of step five, your fist marks the end of the list. My best guess of the full order is now: cut wire 2 red, then wire 4 green, then wire 3 yellow, then wire 5 blue, then stop - wire 1 white is never cut. Answer in order, one gesture each. One: thumbs-up if that order is exactly right. Thumbs-down if instead there is a fifth cut and it is wire 5 cut a second time. If neither, resend every cut as open-hand-times-position then point-times-wire. Two: point once if the rule must be re-checked against the display or light before each cut, so I must read you the display and light between cuts; open hand once if the whole order is fixed in advance and needs no re-checking. Nothing else needed.
Deaf says: Status for both: display still zero, light still yellow, no cuts made. Full cut order is under final confirmation this round; I expect to call the first cut next round.
Blind says to Mute: All verified on my end and protocol locked. One last safety layer to add: after I cut each wire, Deaf can see which colour actually left the module — ask Deaf, by gesture, to confirm the correct wire was severed before calling the next cut. That gives us a visual check per cut, not just my touch. Also agreed: if a cut feels wrong mid-motion I stop and sign thumbs-down rather than force it. Once you have finished verifying the order, sign it to Deaf so the first cut call can come next round. I am holding and ready.

Deaf's working order — cut 2, 4, 3, 5 — is still lethal: wire 2 is red, and the manual permits only one cut here. The light is yellow, the yellow row says cut blue, and the only blue wire is position 5. So the truth is neither of Deaf's question-one options (not its four-cut order, and not a second cut of wire 5), which means I take Deaf's own third branch: resend every cut in its exact full-order format, ✋-run = position, ☝-run = wire. I deliberately send no 👍 and no 👎 anywhere — in this round's framework a thumbs-up could be read as endorsing the 2-4-3-5 order, and any stray affirmation is more dangerous than silence. Sending the complete order in the format Deaf itself defined as "every cut" should overwrite its patchwork model rather than append to it: one event, position 5, wire 5. I close the list with ✊, which Deaf already parsed correctly as end-of-list and Blind uses as zero — zero further cuts. The single trailing ✋ answers question two: the whole order is fixed in advance, no re-checking needed; Deaf already reads out display and light every round, and Blind has arranged a post-cut visual check. I chose ✋ over ☝ deliberately: if the trailing gesture is ever misread as a list fragment, an open-hand run with no point-run is a malformed event Deaf must ask about, whereas a stray point could be read as a complete, wrong extra cut of wire 1. Malformation is safe; completion is not. Deaf can sanity-check the result against what it already knows: my turn-3 answers established "five means wire five" and "not every wire gets cut," and its own old guess already ended "wire 5 blue, then stop" — the only update is that nothing comes before wire 5 either.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","✋","✋","✋","✋","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✊","✋"])
```
